Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ১) Which of the following is normal female karyotype?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
A normal female has 46 chromosomes, including 44 autosomes and two X chromosomes (XX). Therefore, the normal female karyotype is 46,XX.

Rapid Recall

  • Normal female → 46,XX

  • Normal male → 46,XY

  • Turner syndrome → 45,X

  • Klinefelter syndrome → 47,XXY

  • XYY syndrome → 47,XYY

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২) Which one is not a stop codon?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The three stop (termination) codons in the genetic code are:

  • UAA (Ochre)

  • UAG (Amber)

  • UGA (Opal/Umber)

UGG is not a stop codon. It codes for the amino acid tryptophan (Trp).

Rapid Recall

  • Start codon → AUG (Methionine)

  • Stop codons → UAA, UAG, UGA

  • UGG → Tryptophan (not a stop codon)

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৩) DNA replication occurs in which step of cell cycle?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The S (Synthesis) phase of the cell cycle is the stage in which DNA replication occurs. During this phase, each chromosome duplicates to form two identical sister chromatids, preparing the cell for mitosis.

High-Yield Cell Cycle

Phase Major Event
G1 Cell growth, RNA & protein synthesis
S DNA replication, centrosome duplication
G2 Preparation for mitosis, DNA repair
M Mitosis and cytokinesis

Rapid Recall

  • G1 → Growth

  • S → DNA Synthesis (Replication)

  • G2 → Get ready for mitosis

  • M → Mitosis

Mnemonic: G1 → S → G2 → M = Grow → Synthesize DNA → Get ready → Mitosis

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৪) Which of the following is an autosomal recessive condition?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Sickle cell disease is caused by a mutation in the β-globin (HBB) gene on chromosome 11 and is inherited in an autosomal recessive (AR) pattern. Affected individuals inherit one abnormal allele from each parent.

Note: Cystic fibrosis is also an autosomal recessive disorder. If this is intended as a single best answer (SBA), the question is flawed because it has two correct answers.

Rapid Recall

Autosomal Dominant (AD):

  • Marfan syndrome

  • Hereditary spherocytosis

  • Achondroplasia

  • Huntington disease

Autosomal Recessive (AR):

  • Sickle cell disease

  • Cystic fibrosis

  • β-Thalassemia

  • Phenylketonuria (PKU)

Exam Tip: As written, this MCQ has two correct answers (গ and ঘ). It should be revised or converted into a multiple-correct question.

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৫) Which of the following is a primary lymphoid organ?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Primary (central) lymphoid organs are where lymphocytes develop and mature:

  • Bone marrow → B lymphocyte maturation (and origin of all lymphocytes)

  • Thymus → T lymphocyte maturation

Secondary (peripheral) lymphoid organs are where mature lymphocytes encounter antigens and initiate immune responses.

High-Yield Lymphoid Organs

Primary (Central) Secondary (Peripheral)
Bone marrow Spleen
Thymus Lymph nodes
Tonsils
Appendix
Peyer's patches (GALT)

Rapid Recall

  • Primary lymphoid organs → Bone marrow, Thymus

  • Secondary lymphoid organs → Spleen, Lymph nodes, Tonsils, Appendix, Peyer's patches

  • B cells mature in Bone marrow

  • T cells mature in Thymus

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৬) Which immunoglobulin can cross the placenta?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
IgG is the only immunoglobulin that normally crosses the placenta. It is actively transported via the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), providing passive immunity to the fetus and newborn.

Rapid Recall

  • IgG → Crosses placenta

  • IgA → Breast milk & mucosal secretions

  • IgM → First antibody produced

  • IgE → Allergy & parasites

  • IgD → B-cell receptor

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৭) Cellular immunity is mediated by which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Cell-mediated (cellular) immunity is mediated by T lymphocytes. These cells recognize antigen presented by MHC molecules and destroy infected or abnormal cells or coordinate immune responses through cytokine secretion.

Rapid Recall

  • T cells → Cellular immunity

  • B cells → Humoral immunity

  • Plasma cells → Antibody secretion

  • Neutrophils → First responders in acute bacterial infection

  • Basophils → Allergy (histamine)

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৮) Which of the following is the most important part of the clinical decision-making process?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
A careful history is the most important component of clinical decision-making. In most patients, the diagnosis can be suspected or established primarily from the history, with physical examination and investigations used to confirm the diagnosis and assess severity.

High-Yield Clinical Approach

Step Purpose
History Most important for diagnosis
General examination Assess overall condition and vital signs
Systemic examination Localize disease and identify physical signs
Investigations Confirm diagnosis, assess severity, monitor treatment

Rapid Recall

  • History → Most important

  • Examination → Supports diagnosis

  • Investigation → Confirms diagnosis

  • Treat the patient, not the investigation

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৯) ACE inhibitor causes which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
ACE inhibitors (e.g., enalapril, lisinopril, ramipril) can cause renal impairment, particularly in patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis, dehydration, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease. They dilate the efferent arteriole, reducing intraglomerular pressure and potentially lowering GFR.

Rapid Recall

  • ACE inhibitors → Cough, Hyperkalaemia, Angioedema, Renal impairment

  • Contraindicated in bilateral renal artery stenosis

  • Monitor serum creatinine and potassium after initiation

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ১০) Ideal time for taking antihypertensive drug is?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
For most patients, antihypertensive medication is traditionally advised once in the morning to ensure regular daily dosing and improve adherence. Current hypertension guidelines emphasize that the best time is the time the patient can take it consistently, and routine bedtime dosing is not recommended for everyone.

Rapid Recall

  • Antihypertensives → Regular daily dosing

  • Standard MCQ answer → Morning

  • Not taken "when required"

  • Consistency is more important than the exact time

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ১১) Example of type-II hypersensitivity is
১২) Which one is the most common cause of premature mortality globally?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Globally, ischaemic heart disease (IHD) is the leading cause of premature mortality and death. It accounts for the greatest number of years of life lost (YLL) and remains the single largest contributor to global mortality.

Rapid Recall

  • #1 global cause of premature mortality → Ischaemic heart disease

  • #2 → Stroke

  • Leading infectious cause → Lower respiratory infections

  • Leading cause of death in children <5 years → Preterm birth complication

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ১৩) ‘Salmonella’ is a -
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Salmonella is a Gram-negative, motile bacillus (rod) belonging to the family Enterobacteriaceae. It is a facultative intracellular pathogen that causes enteric fever (typhoid/paratyphoid) and gastroenteritis.

Rapid Recall

  • Salmonella → Gram-negative bacillus

  • Motile

  • Non-lactose fermenter

  • H₂S positive

  • Causes typhoid fever and gastroenteritis

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ১৪) ‘Small pupil’ is a feature of which of the following poisoning?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Pinpoint pupils (miosis) are a classic feature of opioid poisoning due to stimulation of the parasympathetic (Edinger–Westphal) nucleus. The classic opioid overdose triad is:

  • Miosis (pinpoint pupils)

  • Respiratory depression

  • Reduced level of consciousness (coma)

Rapid Recall

  • Opioids → Miosis + Respiratory depression + Coma

  • Sympathomimetics (amphetamine, cocaine) → Mydriasis

  • Anticholinergics (TCA, atropine) → Mydriasis

  • Naloxone is the antidote for opioid overdose

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ১৫) Which of the following is the antidote of Paracetamol poisoning?
১৬) Nicotinic feature of OPC poisoning is -
১৭) Hypothermia exists when core temperature falls below which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Hypothermia is defined as a core body temperature below 35°C (95°F). It is classified into mild, moderate, and severe hypothermia based on the core temperature.

High-Yield Classification of Hypothermia

Core Temperature Classification
35–32°C Mild hypothermia
32–28°C Moderate hypothermia
<28°C Severe hypothermia

Rapid Recall

  • Hypothermia = Core temperature <35°C

  • 35–32°C → Mild

  • 32–28°C → Moderate

  • <28°C → Severe

  • Complications: Bradycardia, arrhythmias, hypotension, reduced consciousness.

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ১৮) Which of the following is the most common cause of drowning in Infants or young children?
১৯) Which of the following is a prominent feature of cardiac chest pain?
২০) Fever with Severe headache and photophobia, neck stiffness usually suggestive of which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The combination of fever, severe headache, photophobia, and neck stiffness is the classic presentation of meningitis. Patients may also have altered mental status, vomiting, seizures, and positive Kernig's or Brudzinski's signs.

Rapid Recall

  • Fever + Severe headache + Neck stiffness + Photophobia = Meningitis

  • Classic triad: Fever, neck stiffness, altered mental status

  • Urgent investigations: Blood cultures, lumbar puncture (if no contraindication)

  • Treatment: Prompt empirical IV antibiotics ± dexamethasone.

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২১) Which of the following disease in not transmitted by mosquito bite?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is not transmitted by mosquitoes. It is transmitted by the bite of an infected female sandfly (Phlebotomus spp.). In contrast, malaria, chikungunya, and filariasis are all mosquito-borne diseases.

High-Yield Vector-Borne Diseases

Disease Vector
Malaria Female Anopheles mosquito
Kala-azar (Visceral leishmaniasis) Female Phlebotomus sandfly
Chikungunya Aedes mosquito
Lymphatic filariasis Culex mosquito (most common)

Rapid Recall

  • Malaria → Anopheles mosquito

  • Kala-azar → Sandfly

  • Chikungunya → Aedes mosquito

  • Filariasis → Culex mosquito

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২২) ‘Koplik’s spots’ is pathognomonic for which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Koplik's spots are pathognomonic for measles (rubeola). They appear as small bluish-white spots with a red halo on the buccal mucosa opposite the molars, typically 1–2 days before the characteristic maculopapular rash.

Rapid Recall

  • Koplik's spots → Measles

  • 3 Cs of measles: Cough, Coryza, Conjunctivitis

  • Rash starts on the face and spreads downward

  • Rubella ≠ Measles; Rubella is also called German measles

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২৩) ‘Flushing faint macular rash’ occurs in which days of dengue virus infection?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
In dengue virus infection, a transient flushing or faint macular rash typically appears during the first 1–2 days of illness (febrile phase). A more widespread maculopapular rash often develops later, around days 3–5, as the fever subsides.

High-Yield Timeline of Dengue

Rapid Recall

  • Day 1–2 → Flushing/faint macular rash

  • Day 3–5 → Generalized maculopapular rash

  • Critical phase begins around defervescence (Day 3–7)

  • Warning signs usually appear at the start of the critical phase

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২৪) Treatment should be continued for how many days for enteric fever?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The usual duration of antibiotic treatment for uncomplicated enteric (typhoid) fever is 10–14 days, depending on the antibiotic used. In traditional undergraduate and FCPS-style MCQs, the best answer is 14 days.

Rapid Recall

  • Standard MCQ answer → 14 days

  • Common causes: Salmonella Typhi, Salmonella Paratyphi

  • Diagnosis: Blood culture (best in the first week)

  • Definitive treatment: Appropriate antibiotics guided by local resistance patterns.

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২৫) Which one is the cardinal feature of leprosy?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.option1: Skin lesions, typically anaesthetic at tuberculoid end of spectrum

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২৬) ‘Chlamydia trachomatis’ causes which of the following?
২৭) Which of the following plasmodium species may persist in liver cells as dormant forms?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Plasmodium vivax can persist in liver cells as dormant forms called hypnozoites, which may reactivate weeks to months later, causing relapses. Plasmodium ovale also forms hypnozoites, but it is not listed among the options.

Rapid Recall

  • Hypnozoites → P. vivax and P. ovale

  • Relapse → Due to dormant liver hypnozoites

  • Recrudescence → P. malariae and P. falciparum (persistent blood-stage parasites)

  • Primaquine or tafenoquine is required to eradicate hypnozoites (after excluding G6PD deficiency).

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২৮) Which of the following is the vector of kala-azar?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is caused by Leishmania donovani and is transmitted by the bite of the female sandfly (Phlebotomus argentipes in the Indian subcontinent, including Bangladesh)..

High-Yield Disease–Vector Associations

Disease Vector
Kala-azar (Visceral leishmaniasis) Female sandfly (Phlebotomus)
Malaria Female Anopheles mosquito
Dengue, Chikungunya Aedes aegypti mosquito
Lymphatic filariasis Culex quinquefasciatus mosquito

Rapid Recall

  • Kala-azar → Sandfly

  • Leishmania donovani → Visceral leishmaniasis

  • Malaria → Anopheles

  • Dengue/Chikungunya → Aedes

  • Filariasis → Culex

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ২৯) Which one is the most common route of HIV transmission?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Sexual transmission is the most common route of HIV transmission worldwide. HIV is transmitted through unprotected vaginal or anal intercourse with an infected partner. Mother-to-child transmission (during pregnancy, vaginal delivery, or breastfeeding) and contaminated blood transfusion are other recognized routes but are less common globally.

Rapid Recall

  • Most common HIV transmission → Sexual contact

  • Most efficient transmission → Blood transfusion (unscreened blood)

  • Vertical transmission → Pregnancy, delivery, breastfeeding

  • Prevention of mother-to-child transmission → Maternal ART, infant prophylaxis, and appropriate obstetric/postnatal care

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৩০) Which organism of STI is transmitted through placenta?
৩১) Which of the following is the most common cause of genital ulcer?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Herpes simplex virus (HSV), especially HSV-2, is the most common cause of genital ulcer disease worldwide. Genital herpes typically presents with multiple painful vesicles or ulcers, often associated with tender inguinal lymphadenopathy.

Rapid Recall

  • Most common genital ulcer → HSV

  • Painful ulcer → HSV, chancroid

  • Painless ulcer → Syphilis, LGV, donovanosis

  • Gonorrhea → Urethritis/cervicitis, not genital ulcers

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৩২) Maximum Na reabsorption occurs in which part of nephron?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) reabsorbs the largest proportion of filtered sodium (≈65–70%). Sodium reabsorption here is coupled with the reabsorption of water, glucose, amino acids, bicarbonate, and phosphate, making it the principal site of tubular reabsorption.

Rapid Recall

  • Maximum Na⁺ reabsorption → PCT (65–70%)

  • Loop of Henle → NKCC2 → Loop diuretics

  • DCT → NCC → Thiazides

  • Collecting duct → ENaC → Aldosterone; blocked by amiloride

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৩৩) Which is not a component of Hartmann’s solution?
৩৪) In which of the following condition euvolaemic hyponatraemia occurs?
৩৫) The presence of leucocytes and nitrites in urine is indicative of which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The presence of leukocytes (positive leukocyte esterase) and nitrites in urine is highly suggestive of a urinary tract infection (UTI). Nitrites are formed when nitrate-reducing bacteria (most commonly Escherichia coli) convert urinary nitrates into nitrites.

High-Yield Urine Dipstick Findings

Finding Suggests
Leukocyte esterase Pyuria (WBCs)
Nitrite positive Gram-negative UTI (especially E. coli)
RBC casts Acute glomerulonephritis
Heavy proteinuria Nephrotic syndrome

Rapid Recall

  • Leukocyte esterase + Nitrite → UTI

  • Most common organism → Escherichia coli

  • RBC casts → Acute glomerulonephritis

  • Heavy proteinuria → Nephrotic syndrome

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৩৬) Which of the following is the cause of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN)?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis (RPGN) is a clinical syndrome characterized by a rapid decline in renal function over days to weeks, usually with crescent formation on renal biopsy. It can occur as a severe manifestation of several glomerular diseases, including:

  • IgA nephropathy (crescentic IgA nephropathy)

  • Alport syndrome (rarely, crescentic GN may develop)

  • Post-infectious glomerulonephritis (occasionally progresses to RPGN)

Therefore, all of the listed conditions can cause RPGN.

Option Analysis

  • ক) IgA nephropathy ✔ Can present as crescentic (RPGN) IgA nephropathy.

  • খ) Alport’s syndrome ✔ Rarely associated with crescentic GN/RPGN.

  • গ) Post-infectious glomerulonephritis ✔ May occasionally present as RPGN.

  • ঘ) All above  Correct.

High-Yield Causes of RPGN

Type Common Causes
Type I (Anti-GBM) Goodpasture syndrome
Type II (Immune complex) IgA nephropathy, Post-infectious GN, Lupus nephritis, IgA vasculitis
Type III (Pauci-immune) ANCA-associated vasculitis (GPA, MPA, EGPA)

Rapid Recall

  • Hallmark of RPGN → Crescents on renal biopsy

  • Common causes → Anti-GBM disease, ANCA-associated vasculitis, immune complex GN

  • Immune complex causes include → IgA nephropathy and post-infectious GN

  • Severe crescentic disease can also rarely occur in Alport syndrome

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৩৭) Which one is the pre-renal cause of AKI?
৩৮) Which one is not an indication of dialysis?
৩৯) Giant V wave in JVP is found in which of the following condition?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
A giant V wave in the jugular venous pulse (JVP) is the classical finding in tricuspid regurgitation (TR). During ventricular systole, blood regurgitates from the right ventricle into the right atrium, causing a marked rise in right atrial pressure and producing a prominent (giant) V wave.

High-Yield JVP Findings

JVP Finding Condition
Giant V waves Tricuspid regurgitation
Cannon a waves Complete heart block, AV dissociation
Absent a waves Atrial fibrillation
Prominent a waves Tricuspid stenosis, pulmonary hypertension

Rapid Recall

  • Giant V wave → Tricuspid regurgitation

  • Cannon a wave → Complete heart block

  • Absent a wave → Atrial fibrillation

  • Prominent a wave → Tricuspid stenosis / Pulmonary hypertension

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৪০) ST elevation in II, III, aVF in a 12 lead ECG, indicates which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF indicates an inferior wall myocardial infarction (MI). The inferior wall is usually supplied by the right coronary artery (RCA) (≈80–85% of patients with right-dominant circulation), and less commonly by the left circumflex artery (LCx).

High-Yield ECG Localization

MI Location ECG Leads with ST Elevation Common Artery
Inferior II, III, aVF RCA (most common), LCx
Anterior V1–V4 LAD
Lateral I, aVL, V5–V6 LCx / Diagonal branch
High lateral I, aVL LCx / First diagonal

Rapid Recall

  • II, III, aVF → Inferior MI

  • V1–V4 → Anterior MI

  • I, aVL, V5–V6 → Lateral MI

  • Inferior MI + hypotension → Consider right ventricular infarction; record right-sided leads (especially V4R).

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৪১) Which of the following is the hallmark of angina pectoris?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The hallmark of stable angina pectoris is chest pain or discomfort precipitated by physical exertion or emotional stress and relieved by rest or glyceryl trinitrate (GTN). It results from transient myocardial ischaemia due to an imbalance between myocardial oxygen supply and demand.

Rapid Recall

  • Stable angina → Chest pain on exertion

  • Relieved by rest or GTN

  • Pain at rest → Think unstable angina

  • Typical triad: Exertional pain + Relief with rest + Short duration

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৪২) Which of the following is the most common cause of sudden arrhythmic death?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the most common cause of sudden arrhythmic death (sudden cardiac death) in adults. Most cases result from ventricular tachycardia (VT) or ventricular fibrillation (VF) occurring in the setting of acute myocardial ischaemia or previous myocardial infarction with myocardial scar.

Although structural heart disease is a broad category that includes CAD, the single most common specific cause is coronary artery disease.

Rapid Recall

  • Most common cause of sudden cardiac death → Coronary artery disease

  • Most common mechanism → Ventricular fibrillation

  • Young athletes → Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is a leading cause

  • Inherited non-structural causes → Long QT syndrome, Brugada syndrome, CPVT

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৪৩) Soft first heart sound is found in which of the following condition?
৪৪) Which one of the following is the feature of right heart failure?
৪৫) Physiological cause of Sinus bradycardia is?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Sinus bradycardia is physiological in well-trained athletes due to increased vagal (parasympathetic) tone and enhanced cardiac efficiency. Resting heart rates of 40–60 beats/min (or even lower) may be normal in athletes.

The other options are pathological causes of sinus bradycardia.

High-Yield Causes of Sinus Bradycardia

Physiological Pathological
Athletes Hypothyroidism
Sleep Hypothermia
High vagal tone Inferior MI
Raised intracranial pressure
Drugs (β-blockers, verapamil, diltiazem, digoxin)

Rapid Recall

  • Physiological sinus bradycardia → Athletes, sleep

  • Most common physiological cause → Increased vagal tone

  • Hypothyroidism, hypothermia, drugs → Pathological bradycardia

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৪৬) Which one is a common factors that precipitating angina?
৪৭) Flame-shaped or blot haemorrhages and ‘cotton wool’ exudates are the features of which grade of hyepertensive retinopathy?
৪৮) Which anti-hypertensive is contraindicated in pregnancy?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Ramipril, an ACE inhibitor, is contraindicated in pregnancy, especially during the 2nd and 3rd trimesters, because it can cause fetal renal dysgenesis, oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, skull hypoplasia, neonatal renal failure, and fetal death.

Rapid Recall

  • Contraindicated in pregnancy → ACE inhibitors, ARBs, Aliskiren

  • First-line drugs → Labetalol, Nifedipine, Methyldopa

  • Hydralazine → Severe hypertension in pregnancy

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৪৯) Which one is the minor criteria of rheumatic fever?
৫০) Murmurs of aortic regargitation
৫১) ‘Stony dull’ Percussion note is a typical examination finding of which of the following?
৫২) ‘Increased translucency’ in x-ray found in which of the following condition?
৫৩) Productive cough, changes in posture induce sputum production is a typical feature of which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Bronchiectasis is characterized by a chronic productive cough with large volumes of purulent sputum. A typical feature is that changing posture (postural drainage) often induces the expectoration of sputum because secretions pool within the abnormally dilated bronchi.

Rapid Recall

  • Bronchiectasis → Copious purulent sputum + Postural drainage

  • Diagnosis of choice → High-resolution CT (HRCT) chest

  • Common causes → Previous infection, cystic fibrosis, primary ciliary dyskinesia, immunodeficiency

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৫৪) Exudative pleural effusion found in which of the following condition?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Exudative pleural effusion results from increased capillary permeability or pleural inflammation. Pulmonary infarction (usually due to pulmonary embolism) causes pleural inflammation and therefore produces an exudative pleural effusion.

In contrast, heart failure, liver failure (hepatic hydrothorax), and renal failure usually cause transudative pleural effusions due to increased hydrostatic pressure or decreased oncotic pressure.

High-Yield Causes of Pleural Effusion

Transudate Exudate
Heart failure Pulmonary infarction (PE)
Liver cirrhosis Pneumonia (parapneumonic effusion)
Nephrotic syndrome Tuberculosis
Hypoalbuminaemia Malignancy

Rapid Recall

  • Transudate → Heart failure, Cirrhosis, Nephrotic syndrome

  • Exudate → Infection, Malignancy, Pulmonary embolism/infarction, TB

  • Light's criteria are used to distinguish transudative from exudative pleural effusions.

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৫৫) Which one is the feature of acute severe asthma?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.option4: Inability to complete sentences in 1 breath
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
According to BTS/SIGN and GINA guidelines, acute severe asthma is diagnosed if any one of the following is present:

  • PEF 33–50% of predicted or best

  • Respiratory rate ≥25/min

  • Heart rate ≥110/min

  • Inability to complete sentences in one breath

A PEF <33% predicted indicates life-threatening asthma, not merely acute severe asthma.


Rapid Recall

  • Acute severe asthma: PEF 33–50%, RR ≥25/min, HR ≥110/min, cannot complete sentences

  • Life-threatening asthma: PEF <33%, silent chest, cyanosis, normal/rising PaCO₂, altered consciousness

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৫৬) In stage II COPD, predicted FEV1% is
৫৭) Regarding CURB-65% score, which one is correct?
৫৮) Which anti-TB drug causes hyperuricaemia?
৫৯) Which lung cancer is most common in male smoker?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Squamous cell carcinoma is the lung cancer classically associated with cigarette smoking, especially in male smokers. It usually arises centrally from the major bronchi and may present with cavitation or hypercalcaemia due to PTHrP production.

Exam point: Although adenocarcinoma is now the most common lung cancer overall, including in many smokers, BCPS/FCPS and traditional exam questions asking for the most common lung cancer in a male smoker generally expect Squamous cell carcinoma.

High-Yield Comparison

Type Smoking Association Typical Location Characteristic Feature
Squamous cell Strong Central Cavitation, PTHrP → Hypercalcaemia
Adenocarcinoma Weak–moderate Peripheral Most common overall
Small-cell Very strong Central SIADH, ACTH, Lambert–Eaton syndrome
Large-cell Variable Peripheral Poorly differentiated

Rapid Recall

  • Male smoker → Squamous cell carcinoma

  • Overall most common lung cancer → Adenocarcinoma

  • Strongest smoking association → Small-cell carcinoma

  • Hypercalcaemia (PTHrP) → Squamous cell carcinoma

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৬০) ‘Diffuse firm goitre’ is a typical feature of which of the following?
৬১) Which endocrine disease causes weight gain?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Cushing's syndrome is characterized by progressive weight gain, particularly central (truncal) obesity, due to excess cortisol. Other features include moon face, buffalo hump, proximal muscle weakness, purple striae, hypertension, and glucose intolerance.

High-Yield Weight Change in Endocrine Disorders

Disorder Weight Change
Cushing's syndrome Weight gain (central obesity)
Hypothyroidism Weight gain
Thyrotoxicosis Weight loss
Adrenal insufficiency Weight loss
Diabetes mellitus (untreated) Weight loss

Rapid Recall

  • Weight gain + moon face + buffalo hump → Cushing's syndrome

  • Weight gain + cold intolerance → Hypothyroidism

  • Weight loss + heat intolerance → Thyrotoxicosis

  • Weight loss + hyperpigmentation + hypotension → Addison's disease

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৬২) Which one is the feature of turner’s syndrome?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Turner syndrome is a chromosomal disorder affecting females, caused by complete or partial monosomy X. The classic karyotype is 45,XO. Typical features include short stature, webbed neck, shield chest, streak ovaries, primary amenorrhoea, and infertility.

High-Yield Features of Turner Syndrome

Feature Turner Syndrome
Karyotype 45,XO
Sex Female
Stature Short
Gonads Streak ovaries
Puberty Primary amenorrhoea, delayed puberty
Associated anomalies Coarctation of aorta, bicuspid aortic valve, horseshoe kidney

Rapid Recall

  • Turner syndrome → 45,XO

  • Short stature + webbed neck + streak ovaries

  • Primary amenorrhoea and infertility

  • Associated with coarctation of the aorta and horseshoe kidn

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question:
৬৩)

Prednisolone 5 mg is approximately equivalent to which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The standard glucocorticoid equivalent doses are:

Corticosteroid Equivalent Dose
Hydrocortisone 20 mg
Cortisone acetate 25 mg
Prednisolone 5 mg
Methylprednisolone 4 mg
Deflazacort 6–7.5 mg
Dexamethasone 0.75 mg

Therefore, Prednisolone 5 mg is equivalent to both:

  • Hydrocortisone 20 mg

  • Dexamethasone 0.75 mg

Rapid Recall

  • Hydrocortisone 20 mg = Prednisolone 5 mg = Dexamethasone 0.75 mg

  • Cortisone acetate 25 mg = Prednisolone 5 mg

  • Deflazacort 6–7.5 mg ≈ Prednisolone 5 mg

Exam tip: This question has two correct options (ক and খ). For a single best answer (SBA), modify one distractor. For example:

Prednisolone 5 mg is approximately equivalent to:

  • A. Hydrocortisone 20 mg ✅

  • B. Dexamethasone 0.5 mg

  • C. Cortisone acetate 50 mg

  • D. Deflazacort 3 mg

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৬৪) Which of the following is an essential amino acid?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Methionine is an essential amino acid, meaning it cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained from the diet. It is a sulfur-containing amino acid and serves as the precursor of S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), an important methyl group donor.

High-Yield Essential Amino Acids

Mnemonic: PVT TIM HALL

  • P – Phenylalanine

  • V – Valine

  • T – Threonine

  • T – Tryptophan

  • I – Isoleucine

  • M – Methionine

  • H – Histidine

  • A – (Arginine – essential during growth/children)

  • L – Leucine

  • L – Lysine

Rapid Recall

  • Methionine → Essential, sulfur-containing amino acid

  • Serine, Glutamate → Non-essential amino acids

  • Choline → Essential nutrient, not an amino acid

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৬৫) Deficiency of which vitamin causes pellagra?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Pellagra is caused by niacin (Vitamin B3) deficiency or deficiency of its precursor, tryptophan. It is classically characterized by the 3 Ds:

  • Dermatitis (photosensitive)

  • Diarrhoea

  • Dementia

If untreated, it may progress to the 4th D – Death.

High-Yield Vitamin Deficiencies

Vitamin Deficiency Disease
B1 (Thiamin) Beriberi, Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome
B2 (Riboflavin) Cheilosis, angular stomatitis, glossitis
B3 (Niacin) Pellagra (3 Ds)
B7 (Biotin) Dermatitis, alopecia

Rapid Recall

  • Niacin (B3) deficiency → Pellagra

  • Pellagra = 3 Ds: Dermatitis, Diarrhoea, Dementia

  • Tryptophan deficiency can also cause pellagra

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৬৬) Diabetes is confirmed by which of the following criteria?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.option3: 2-hr glucose after 75 g oral glucose drink 7.8 - 11.1 mmol/L

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৬৭) Which one is the indicator of severe DKA?
৬৮) Which anti diabetic drug may produce hypoglycaemia?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Sulphonylureas (e.g., gliclazide, glimepiride, glibenclamide) stimulate insulin secretion from pancreatic β-cells regardless of blood glucose level. Therefore, they carry a significant risk of hypoglycaemia, especially in elderly patients, those with renal impairment, or when meals are skipped.

High-Yield Antidiabetic Drugs and Hypoglycaemia

Drug Class Risk of Hypoglycaemia
Sulphonylureas High
Insulin High
Metformin Minimal
DPP-4 inhibitors Minimal
SGLT2 inhibitors Minimal
GLP-1 receptor agonists Minimal
Thiazolidinediones Minimal

Rapid Recall

  • Sulphonylureas → ↑ Insulin secretion → Hypoglycaemia

  • Metformin → No hypoglycaemia (monotherapy)

  • SGLT2 inhibitors → Genital infections, euglycaemic DKA

  • DPP-4 inhibitors → Weight neutral, low hypoglycaemia risk

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৬৯) Which hormone stimulates gastric acid secretion?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Gastrin is the principal hormone that stimulates gastric acid (HCl) secretion by parietal cells, mainly indirectly through enterochromaffin-like (ECL) cells, which release histamine. Gastrin also promotes gastric mucosal growth and increases gastric motility.

    High-Yield GI Hormones

    Hormone Main Action
    Gastrin ↑ Gastric acid secretion, ↑ gastric mucosal growth
    Secretin ↑ Pancreatic bicarbonate, ↓ gastric acid secretion
    GIP ↑ Insulin secretion, ↓ gastric acid secretion
    Somatostatin Inhibits gastrin, gastric acid, insulin, glucagon, and many GI hormones

    Rapid Recall

    • Gastrin → "G" for Gastric acid ↑

    • Secretin → Neutralizes acid (↑ HCO₃⁻, ↓ HCl)

    • GIP → Insulin release after oral glucose

    • Somatostatin → Universal inhibitory hormone

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৭০) Which one is the most common cause of upper GIT haemorrhage?
৭১) ‘Night blindness’ is the consequence of which of the following vitamin deficiency?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Night blindness (nyctalopia) is the earliest manifestation of vitamin A deficiency. Vitamin A is required for the formation of rhodopsin, the visual pigment in retinal rod cells responsible for vision in dim light.

Prolonged deficiency can lead to:

  • Night blindness

  • Conjunctival xerosis

  • Bitot's spots

  • Corneal xerosis

  • Keratomalacia (can lead to blindness)

Rapid Recall

  • Vitamin A → Night blindness

  • Vitamin D → Rickets/Osteomalacia

  • Vitamin E → Neurological deficits

  • Vitamin K → Bleeding

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৭২) Which of the following is the most common type of stomach Cancer?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Adenocarcinoma accounts for approximately 90–95% of all gastric (stomach) cancers, making it the most common histological type. It arises from the glandular epithelium of the gastric mucosa.

Major risk factors include:

  • Helicobacter pylori infection

  • Chronic atrophic gastritis

  • Intestinal metaplasia

  • Smoking

  • High intake of smoked and salted foods

  • Family history

Rapid Recall

  • Most common stomach cancer → Adenocarcinoma

  • H. pylori → Major risk factor

  • Diffuse type → Linitis plastica, CDH1 mutation

  • Intestinal type → Chronic atrophic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৭৩) Which one is the Non-invasive test for H.pylori infection?
৭৪) Ulcerative colitis most commonly affects which part of gut?
৭৫) Which of the following is the most common cause of acute pancreatitis in Bangladesh?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
In Bangladesh, the most common cause of acute pancreatitis is gallstone disease (biliary pancreatitis). Although alcohol is a major cause in many Western countries, gallstones predominate in Bangladesh and most South Asian countries.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Gallstones  Correct. Most common cause of acute pancreatitis in Bangladesh.

  • খ) Alcohol  Common in Western countries but less common than gallstones in Bangladesh.

  • গ) Post-ERCP An important iatrogenic cause but relatively uncommon overall.

  • ঘ) Drugs  Rare cause (e.g., azathioprine, valproate, thiazides).

High-Yield Causes of Acute Pancreatitis

Cause Comment
Gallstones Most common in Bangladesh
Alcohol Most common in many Western countries
Hypertriglyceridaemia Usually when TG >11.3 mmol/L (>1000 mg/dL)
Post-ERCP Common procedure-related cause
Drugs Rare

Rapid Recall

  • Bangladesh → Gallstones = Most common cause

  • Western countries → Alcohol + Gallstones are the two leading causes

  • Remember: "GET SMASHED" for causes of acute pancreatitis (Gallstones, Ethanol, Trauma, Steroids, Mumps, Autoimmune, Scorpion sting, Hypertriglyceridaemia/Hypercalcaemia, ERCP, Drugs)

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৭৬) Which of the following is the investigation of choice for diagnosing gallstone?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Abdominal ultrasonography (USG) is the investigation of choice (first-line test) for diagnosing gallstones (cholelithiasis). It is non-invasive, inexpensive, readily available, and has a sensitivity and specificity >95% for detecting gallbladder stones.

Rapid Recall

  • Gallbladder stones → Ultrasound (Investigation of choice)

  • CBD stones → MRCP (diagnosis), ERCP (treatment)

  • Most gallstones are radiolucent → Not seen on plain X-ray

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৭৭) Which factor can precipitate hepatic encephalopathy?
৭৮) Most common route of HBV transmission is
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp: Vertical (mother-to-child) transmission is the most common route of hepatitis B virus (HBV) transmission worldwide, particularly in high-prevalence regions such as Bangladesh and other parts of Asia. Transmission usually occurs during childbirth (perinatal transmission). Without immunoprophylaxis, infants born to HBsAg-positive/HBeAg-positive mothers have a very high risk of acquiring HBV and developing chronic infection.

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৭৯) Which drug causes hepatic fibrosis?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp: Methotrexate can cause chronic hepatotoxicity, leading to hepatic fibrosis and, in some patients, cirrhosis, particularly with long-term use and high cumulative doses. The risk is increased in patients with alcohol use, obesity, diabetes mellitus, and pre-existing liver disease.

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৮০) Which of the following condition(s) haemoglobin–oxygen dissociation curve is Shifted to the left?
৮১) Which of the following is the most common type of anaemia worldwide?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Iron deficiency anaemia (IDA) is the most common type of anaemia worldwide. It is usually caused by chronic blood loss, inadequate dietary iron intake, increased iron requirements (e.g., pregnancy), or malabsorption.

Typical laboratory findings:

  • Low serum ferritin (earliest and most specific indicator of iron deficiency)

  • Low serum iron

  • High total iron-binding capacity (TIBC)

  • Low transferrin saturation

  • Microcytic, hypochromic anaemia

High-Yield Comparison

Anaemia MCV Characteristic Finding
Iron deficiency ↓ (Microcytic) Low ferritin, high TIBC
B12 deficiency ↑ (Macrocytic) Hypersegmented neutrophils, neurological features
Haemolytic Normal/↑ ↑ Reticulocytes, ↑ LDH, ↓ Haptoglobin
Sideroblastic Usually ↓ Ring sideroblasts in bone marrow

Rapid Recall

  • Most common anaemia worldwide → Iron deficiency anaemia

  • Most common cause → Chronic blood loss (adults), poor intake/increased requirement

  • Best initial test → Serum ferritin

  • Blood film → Microcytic, hypochromic RBCs

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৮২) Which antibody present in plasma in a person with blood group ‘AB’?
৮৩) Which one is the hallmark of hemolysis?
৮৪) Which one is the most common type of leukaemia?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia (CLL) is the most common type of leukaemia in adults, particularly in older individuals (usually >60 years). It is characterized by the accumulation of mature but dysfunctional B lymphocytes.

High-Yield Leukaemia Facts

Type Key Point
CLL Most common adult leukaemia; mature B cells; older age
ALL Most common childhood leukaemia
AML Most common acute leukaemia in adults
CML Philadelphia chromosome, BCR-ABL fusion

Rapid Recall

  • Adult most common leukaemia → CLL

  • Child most common leukaemia → ALL

  • Most common acute leukaemia in adults → AML

  • Philadelphia chromosome → CML

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৮৫) Which one causes acute monoarthritis?
৮৬) ‘Felty’s syndrome’ is associated with which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Felty’s syndrome is a rare complication of long-standing, severe seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. It is characterized by the triad:

  • Rheumatoid arthritis

  • Neutropenia

  • Splenomegaly

Patients are at increased risk of recurrent infections due to neutropenia.

Option Analysis

  • ক) RA ✔ Correct. Felty’s syndrome is associated with long-standing RA.

  • খ) SLE  SLE may cause cytopenias but is not associated with Felty’s syndrome.

  • গ) OA  Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease and does not cause Felty’s syndrome.

  • ঘ) Gout Gout is a crystal arthropathy and has no association with Felty’s syndrome.

High-Yield Felty’s Syndrome

Feature Finding
Associated disease Rheumatoid arthritis
Triad RA + Neutropenia + Splenomegaly
Typical patient Long-standing, severe, seropositive RA
Main complication Recurrent bacterial infections

Rapid Recall

  • Felty = RA + Splenomegaly + Neutropenia

  • F → Felty → Five letters: think RA

  • Most common autoimmune arthritis → RA

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৮৭) Root value of Ankle jerk is?
৮৮) Which cell of CNS derives from monocytes?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Microglial cells are the resident macrophages of the central nervous system (CNS) and are derived from monocyte/macrophage lineage (mesoderm). They act as immune cells of the CNS and perform phagocytosis, antigen presentation, and inflammatory responses.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Oligodendrocytes  Derived from neural tube (neuroectoderm); responsible for myelin formation in the CNS.

  • খ) Microglial cells ✔ Correct. Derived from monocytes/yolk sac macrophage lineage.

  • গ) Ependymal cells Derived from neuroectoderm; line the ventricles and produce CSF (via choroid plexus).

  • ঘ) Astrocyte Derived from neuroectoderm; provide structural and metabolic support.

High-Yield CNS Cells

Cell Origin Function
Microglia Mesoderm/monocyte lineage CNS macrophage, immune defence
Astrocyte Neuroectoderm Support, blood–brain barrier
Oligodendrocyte Neuroectoderm CNS myelin formation
Ependymal cell Neuroectoderm CSF production/circulation

Rapid Recall

  • Microglia = macrophage of CNS

  • Only CNS glial cell derived from mesoderm

  • Oligodendrocytes → CNS myelin

  • Schwann cells → PNS myelin

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৮৯) Which one is the sign of upper motor neuron lesion?
৯০) Which is not a clinical syndrome of Parkinson disease?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The cardinal clinical features of Parkinson disease are:

  • Bradykinesia (essential for diagnosis)

  • Resting tremor

  • Rigidity

  • Postural instability (usually later)

Sensory loss is not a typical feature of Parkinson disease and suggests involvement of peripheral nerves, spinal cord, or other neurological disorders.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Tremor  A classic feature of Parkinson disease (usually resting tremor).

  • খ) Rigidity  A cardinal feature (classically lead-pipe rigidity or cogwheel rigidity).

  • গ) Sensory loss  Correct. Not a typical Parkinsonian feature.

  • ঘ) Bradykinesia  A core diagnostic feature of Parkinson disease.

Rapid Recall

  • Parkinson triad → Tremor + Rigidity + Bradykinesia

  • Sensory loss → Think peripheral neuropathy, not Parkinson disease

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৯১) Which one causes meningitis in pre-school child?
৯২) ‘Rosier scale’ is associated with which of the following?
৯৩) Which one is an organic mental disorder?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Delirium is an organic mental disorder caused by an underlying medical, neurological, toxic, or metabolic condition. It is characterized by acute onset, fluctuating disturbance of consciousness, impaired attention, and cognitive dysfunction.

Common causes include:

  • Infection (e.g., sepsis)

  • Drugs/toxins

  • Metabolic disturbances

  • Organ failure

Option Analysis

  • ক) Schizophrenia  A functional psychotic disorder, not classified as an organic mental disorder.

  • খ) Sexual dysfunction  A psychiatric/psychosexual disorder, not an organic mental disorder.

  • গ) Delirium ✔ Correct. An acute organic brain syndrome.

  • ঘ) Autism  A neurodevelopmental disorder, not an organic mental disorder in this classification.

High-Yield Organic Mental Disorders

Disorder Key Feature
Delirium Acute confusion + impaired attention + fluctuating consciousness
Dementia Progressive cognitive decline with preserved consciousness initially
Amnestic disorders Memory impairment due to brain dysfunction

Rapid Recall

  • Delirium = Acute organic brain syndrome

  • Dementia = Chronic organic brain syndrome

  • Schizophrenia = Functional psychotic disorder

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৯৪) Which one is a major risk factor for stroke?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
The major risk factors for stroke include:

  • Hypertension (most important modifiable risk factor)

  • Atrial fibrillation

  • Diabetes mellitus

  • Smoking

  • Dyslipidaemia

  • Increasing age

  • Previous stroke/TIA

Among the given options, none represents a major established stroke risk factor.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Female gender  Not a major risk factor. Stroke risk is generally higher in men at younger ages, although women have more strokes overall due to longer life expectancy.

  • খ) Recent divorce  Psychosocial stress may be associated with cardiovascular risk but is not a major stroke risk factor.

  • গ) Young age  Stroke risk increases with advancing age.

  • ঘ) Joint family  Not a stroke risk factor.

High-Yield Stroke Risk Factors

Non-modifiable

  • Age

  • Previous stroke/TIA

  • Family history

  • Sex

Modifiable

  • Hypertension ⭐

  • Atrial fibrillation

  • Diabetes mellitus

  • Smoking

  • Hyperlipidaemia

  • Obesity and physical inactivity

Rapid Recall

  • Most important risk factor for stroke → Hypertension

  • Most common cause of cardioembolic stroke → Atrial fibrillation

  • Stroke risk increases markedly with age

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৯৫) Which drug is used for anxiety disorders?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
Antidepressants, particularly SSRIs (Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors) and SNRIs (Serotonin–Noradrenaline Reuptake Inhibitors), are the first-line pharmacological treatment for most anxiety disorders (e.g., generalized anxiety disorder, panic disorder, social anxiety disorder, OCD).

They are preferred because they provide long-term control and have a lower risk of dependence compared with benzodiazepines.

Option Analysis

  • ক) Antipsychotics  Not first-line treatment; may be used only in specific resistant cases or when psychotic symptoms are present.

  • খ) Antidepressants  Correct. SSRIs/SNRIs are first-line drugs.

  • গ) Sedatives  Benzodiazepines can provide short-term relief but are not preferred for long-term management due to dependence and tolerance.

  • ঘ) No drug is used  Incorrect; medications are commonly used along with psychological therapies.

Rapid Recall

  • Chronic anxiety → SSRI/SNRI

  • Acute anxiety → Benzodiazepine (short-term)

  • Avoid long-term benzodiazepines → dependence risk

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৯৬) Conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol to vitamin D occurs in which of the following site?
৯৭) ‘comedone’ is a typical feature of which of the following?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
A comedone is a typical feature of acne vulgaris. It occurs due to follicular plugging with sebum and keratin.

Types of comedones:

  • Open comedone (blackhead) → oxidized melanin/sebum at the surface

  • Closed comedone (whitehead) → blocked follicle beneath intact skin

Rapid Recall

  • Comedone → Acne

  • Burrow → Scabies

  • Vesicle + itch → Eczema

  • Silvery scale → Psoriasis

Subject Final-01 - Medicine.question: ৯৮) Which of the following condition causes central cyanosis?
৯৯) CVS cause of haemoptysis is
১০০) SKin prick test is associated with wihich type of hypersensitivity reaction?
Subject Final-01 - Medicine.exp:
A skin prick test is used to detect immediate hypersensitivity reactions, which are mediated by IgE antibodies. Therefore, it is associated with Type-I hypersensitivity.

Mechanism:
Allergen exposure → IgE binding to mast cells → Mast cell degranulation → Histamine release → Wheal and flare reaction

Rapid Recall

  • Skin prick test → Type I → IgE

  • Mantoux test → Type IV → T lymphocyte

  • Anaphylaxis → Type I
